map_metadata.name: Harrowgate Grid
map_metadata.description: Primary grid map for Harrowgate, Oregon. A coastal Pacific Northwest city dominated by hydroelectric baseload, a retiring coal station, offshore wind, and an HVDC export link to California.

generation_nodes.name: Vantara River Hydroelectric Dam
generation_nodes.notes: Primary baseload anchor. Large reservoir provides multi-day storage buffer. Spring snowmelt peaks. Winter ice reduces output.

generation_nodes.name: Harrowgate Coastal Coal Station
generation_nodes.notes: Aging subcritical unit scheduled for retirement. Very high emissions. Slow ramp. Kept as backup to hydro during drought. Politically sensitive.

generation_nodes.name: Harrowgate Combined Cycle Gas Plant
generation_nodes.notes: Primary load-following unit. Replaces coal on clean dispatch order. Also serves as backup if hydro output is curtailed.

generation_nodes.name: Cape Harrow Offshore Wind Farm
generation_nodes.notes: Offshore turbines benefit from consistent Pacific winds. Higher cut-out threshold than onshore. Subsea cable connects to coastal substation. Maintenance access weather-dependent.

generation_nodes.name: Harrowgate Valley Solar Farm
generation_nodes.notes: Sited in the rain shadow east of the coastal range. Higher capacity factor than typical Oregon coast. Marine cloud layer reduces summer afternoon output.

generation_nodes.name: Harrowgate Peaker Plant A
generation_nodes.notes: Fast-start emergency and peak unit. High cost and emissions. Dispatched only when hydro and CCGT cannot cover demand.

generation_nodes.name: Harrowgate Peaker Plant B
generation_nodes.notes: Twin to Peaker A. Sharing gas supply and output line to SUB-001.

generation_nodes.name: Harrowgate Waste-to-Energy Station
generation_nodes.notes: Processes city waste stream. Contractually obligated minimum output. Slow ramp. Provides north district baseload. Politically protected.

storage_nodes.name: Harrowgate Grid Battery - Downtown
storage_nodes.notes: Fast-response frequency regulation and wind smoothing. Sited at downtown substation for voltage support.

storage_nodes.name: Vantara Pumped Hydro Storage
storage_nodes.notes: Shares water infrastructure with GEN-001. Uses overnight hydro surplus and off-peak wind to pump. Discharges into morning and evening demand peaks.

substation_nodes.name: Harrowgate Central Transmission Substation
substation_nodes.notes: Main 500/138kV hub. All large generation and the HVDC export feed through here. Most critical single asset on the grid.

substation_nodes.name: North Harrowgate Substation
substation_nodes.notes: Feeds northern residential and the university campus. Also collects waste-to-energy output.

substation_nodes.name: Downtown Harrowgate Substation
substation_nodes.notes: Highest load density node. Feeds CBD, hospital, and data centers. Battery STG-001 co-located here.

substation_nodes.name: Port Industrial Substation
substation_nodes.notes: Serves the deep-water port and heavy industrial zone. Co-located with coal station bus. High flat load 24/7.

substation_nodes.name: South Residential Substation
substation_nodes.notes: Single busbar is a flagged vulnerability. N-1 upgrade deferred to 2026 budget cycle. Loss affects 26,000 southern residents.

substation_nodes.name: East Industrial Substation
substation_nodes.notes: Serves eastern industrial and logistics park. High continuous loading expected.

substation_nodes.name: Coastal Offshore Wind Substation
substation_nodes.notes: Collects offshore wind via subsea cable and steps up for transmission. Also serves coastal marina and airport zone.

substation_nodes.name: Vantara Hydro Generator Step-Up Yard
substation_nodes.notes: Steps up hydro output to 500kV. Transformers refurbished 2018. Loss of one transformer reduces transmission capacity by 50%.

substation_nodes.name: HVDC Export Converter Substation
substation_nodes.notes: HVDC link to California grid. Exports clean hydro and wind surplus. Direction controlled by system operator. Import available up to 400MW in emergencies.

transmission_lines.name: Hydro Dam GSU Connection
transmission_lines.notes: Generator step-up transformer connection, GEN-001 to switchyard

transmission_lines.name: Vantara-Central 500kV Line A
transmission_lines.notes: Long mountain traverse. Double circuit. Ice loading a risk in winter. Primary hydro output pathway.

transmission_lines.name: Vantara-Central 500kV Line B
transmission_lines.notes: Alternate route to TL-001, slightly longer. Both must trip to fully isolate hydro from grid.

transmission_lines.name: Central-Export HVDC 500kV
transmission_lines.notes: Single circuit AC feeder to HVDC converter. Loss eliminates all export and emergency import capability immediately.

transmission_lines.name: Central-East Industrial 138kV
transmission_lines.notes: Double circuit to eastern industrial zone.

transmission_lines.name: Central-Downtown 138kV
transmission_lines.notes: Critical downtown feed. Double circuit. Loss of one creates cascade overload risk.

transmission_lines.name: Coal Station-Central 138kV
transmission_lines.notes: Coal output first routes to port substation bus before connecting upward to central. Shared bus with port industrial.

transmission_lines.name: Port Industrial-Central 138kV
transmission_lines.notes: Carries coal output and port load to/from central substation.

transmission_lines.name: CCGT-Central 138kV
transmission_lines.notes: CCGT output line. Double circuit handles up to 500MW.

transmission_lines.name: Offshore Wind-Coastal Substation 138kV
transmission_lines.notes: Subsea XLPE cable from offshore array to coastal substation. Single circuit - loss curtails all offshore wind. Repair time measured in weeks.

transmission_lines.name: Coastal-Central 138kV
transmission_lines.notes: Brings offshore wind and coastal load zone to main grid.

transmission_lines.name: Central-North Harrowgate 138kV
transmission_lines.notes: North backbone feed. Waste-to-energy also injects at north substation.

transmission_lines.name: Downtown-South Residential 138kV
transmission_lines.notes: Single circuit. Aging infrastructure. A fault here isolates SUB-005 which has no N-1 capability - cascaded failure risk.

transmission_lines.name: East Industrial-Coastal 138kV Ring
transmission_lines.notes: Ring tie installed during offshore wind project. Allows partial rerouting if TL-009 trips.

transmission_lines.name: Peakers-Central 138kV
transmission_lines.notes: Shared output line for both Peaker A and B.

transmission_lines.name: Peaker B-Central 138kV
transmission_lines.notes: Parallel to TL-013 for Peaker B.

transmission_lines.name: Pumped Hydro-Central 138kV
transmission_lines.notes: Long mountain line shared with hydro corridor. Bidirectional. High impedance due to terrain.

transmission_lines.name: North-Downtown 138kV Ring
transmission_lines.notes: Ring tie allowing north-south rerouting if central substation is partially lost.

distribution_lines.name: Hospital Dedicated Feeder
distribution_lines.notes: Dedicated protected feeder. Never to be interrupted.

distribution_lines.name: Harrowgate Airport Dedicated Feeder
distribution_lines.notes: Critical facility. Airport has 15MW backup diesel but prefers grid supply.

distribution_lines.name: Battery Storage-Downtown Feeder
distribution_lines.notes: Bidirectional. Battery co-located at downtown substation site.

distribution_lines.name: Control Center Main Feeder
distribution_lines.notes: Provides main control center with power.

distribution_lines.name: Backup Control Center Feeder
distribution_lines.notes: Backup CC fed from downtown substation rather than central - intentional geographic separation.

load_nodes.name: North Harrowgate Residential
load_nodes.notes: Older suburb. High A/C load in summer. Mild winters. EV penetration 24%.

load_nodes.name: Harrowgate University & Tech Campus
load_nodes.notes: University research labs, data centers, and tech startup campus. Significant 24/7 server load. Critical to city economy.

load_nodes.name: Harrowgate Central Business District
load_nodes.notes: CBD including city hall, offices, retail, and financial district. Summer air conditioning is dominant peak driver.

load_nodes.name: Harrowgate Regional Medical Center
load_nodes.notes: Regional trauma and cancer center. Must never lose supply. Diesel backup covers essential life safety systems only.

load_nodes.name: Harrowgate Deep Water Port & Shipyard
load_nodes.notes: Deep-water container and bulk cargo port. Drydock facilities draw large arc furnace loads. Some interruptible shore-power contracts.

load_nodes.name: South Harrowgate Residential A
load_nodes.notes: Newer suburb with good insulation. SUB-005 has no N-1 capability - loss of one transformer blacks out this entire area.

load_nodes.name: South Harrowgate Residential B & Retail
load_nodes.notes: Mixed retail and residential. Also supplied by co-located rooftop solar (not modelled). Vulnerable via SUB-005 single point of failure.

load_nodes.name: East Harrowgate Industrial & Logistics Park
load_nodes.notes: Cold storage, food processing, and distribution warehouses. 24/7 refrigeration load is largely inflexible. Interruptible non-critical process loads available.

load_nodes.name: Coastal Marina & Residential
load_nodes.notes: Upmarket coastal zone with marina, restaurants, and residential. High summer tourism peak. Shore power demand from recreational vessels.

load_nodes.name: Harrowgate Regional Airport
load_nodes.notes: Regional domestic and international airport. Critical 24/7. Backup diesel covers essential navigation and terminal systems only.

interconnects.name: Harrowgate-California HVDC Interconnect
interconnects.notes: Primary export pathway for clean hydro and wind surplus. California pays premium for renewable certificates. Import available during hydro drought or major generation loss.

gas_infrastructure.name: Harrowgate Natural Gas Transmission Line
gas_infrastructure.notes: Single pipeline feed. No redundancy. Coastal seismic zone makes rupture risk real. A fault simultaneously disables CCGT and both peakers - 860MW of gas generation lost.

backup_control_center.name: Harrowgate Backup Control Center
backup_control_center.notes: Hot standby. Fed from downtown substation rather than central substation for geographic separation.

scada_and_monitoring.notes: Phasor Measurement Units on critical nodes. Offshore wind PMU provides sub-second synchrophasor data for wind ramp detection.

grid_challenges.name: Summer Cooling Peak
grid_challenges.trigger: season == summer AND hour >= 14 AND hour <= 19
grid_challenges.description: Pacific Coast summer heatwaves push residential and commercial A/C load to system peak above 2100MW. Hydro output is derated due to reduced river flow.

grid_challenges.name: Hydro Drought Curtailment
grid_challenges.description: Extended dry season reduces GEN-001 to 40% capacity. Coal must run at full output with CCGT and imports to cover. Emissions spike and export revenue collapses.
grid_challenges.mitigation: Run coal at full output. Maximise CCGT. Import via IC-001. Shed interruptible industrial loads if necessary.

grid_challenges.name: Offshore Wind Ramp Event
grid_challenges.description: Rapid change in offshore wind speed drops GEN-004 from near-full to near-zero in under 20 minutes. 350MW lost with no warning from forecast.
grid_challenges.mitigation: Deploy STG-001 immediately. Ramp GEN-003 CCGT. Hydro can respond in 3 minutes.

grid_challenges.name: Gas Pipeline Disruption
grid_challenges.description: All gas generation (GEN-003, GEN-006, GEN-007) trips simultaneously. 860MW of flexible generation lost.
grid_challenges.mitigation: Maximise hydro immediately. Emergency import via IC-001. Accept coal output. Shed interruptible industrial load.

grid_challenges.name: South Substation Single Point of Failure
grid_challenges.description: SUB-005 has no N-1 capability. Single transformer failure blacks out LOAD-006 and LOAD-007 - 24,000 households.
grid_challenges.mitigation: Partial reroute via TL-011 from SUB-003 but at severely reduced capacity. Demand management required.

grid_challenges.name: Subsea Cable Fault
grid_challenges.description: Loss of the single subsea cable from the offshore wind farm cuts all 350MW of offshore wind instantly. Repair takes 3-6 weeks.
grid_challenges.mitigation: Ramp CCGT to full. Consider running coal alongside. Reduce export target. Monitor frequency closely.

grid_challenges.name: Coal Retirement Transition
grid_challenges.description: Coal station must be taken offline. Without GEN-002 the grid has 40% less thermal inertia. Frequency stability becomes fragile.
grid_challenges.mitigation: Ensure STG-001 and STG-002 are well-charged. CCGT must absorb all load-following. Consider increasing HVDC import capability.

events.name: Sudden Hydro Trip
events.description: Generator protection trip at Vantara Dam. 800MW lost instantaneously. With no nuclear inertia, frequency drops sharply. Coal and gas must respond immediately.

events.name: Pacific Heatwave
events.description: Multi-day high pressure dome. Demand surges 15-20% as residential and commercial A/C loads spike. River temperatures rise reducing hydro efficiency.

events.name: Container Ship Shore Power Demand
events.description: Large container vessel docks and connects to shore power, significantly increasing port demand.

events.name: Mountain Ice Storm
events.description: Ice accumulation on the long mountain transmission lines causes conductor sag and flashover. The hydro corridor lines are especially at risk.

events.name: Cyberattack on SCADA
events.description: Nation-state actor targets the control center. Random line trips triggered. Switch to backup control center to isolate the attack.

events.name: Seismic Event - Pipeline Risk
events.description: Coastal seismic zone earthquake triggers automatic pipeline isolation. All gas generation trips simultaneously. Major dispatch crisis.

events.name: Offshore Wind Maintenance Outage
events.description: Annual offshore maintenance window. Crew transfer weather windows limit access. Entire offshore farm offline.

residential.description: Pacific Northwest residential load. Summer cooling peak. Milder winters than interior. EV charging evening bump.

commercial.description: Office, retail, government. Strong midday summer peak from cooling. Near-zero overnight.

industrial.description: Manufacturing and logistics. Near-flat with slight overnight reduction.

flat.description: Critical infrastructure. Constant load regardless of time.

port_industrial.description: Port operations. High daytime vessel activity, reduced overnight.

airport.description: Airport operations. Two peaks aligned with flight schedules.

mixed_residential_commercial.description: Blend of residential and commercial. Summer afternoon peak.

winter.description: Mild Pacific winters. Modest heating load. Wet season increases hydro river flow but reduces solar.

spring.description: Cool and wet. Lowest demand season. Peak hydro output from snowmelt. Best conditions for export.

summer.description: Heatwaves drive significant A/C load unlike typical Pacific Northwest history. Marine push events create rapid demand swings. Reduced hydro.

autumn.description: Transitional. Storm season begins. Wind output increases. Demand moderate.
